title: Subeg Singh Is Briefed with Gifts, Jagir, and Nawabship Terms

blocks.text: Aslam Khan now spells out what Subeg Singh must say. He is to congratulate the Khalsa for removing a burden from Lahore, speak of mutual advantage, and persuade them that negotiated recognition would serve both sides better than another round of open warfare.

The offer becomes concrete through land, cash, and promises of settled authority. Subeg Singh is instructed to speak of jagir arrangements, local peace, and continuing goodwill, all designed to draw the Panth into a relationship the Lahore administration can manage rather than fear.

The most delicate part of the mission concerns honor and rank. Subeg Singh, carrying the proposal, also receives robes and documents of nawabship, symbols of royal favor that can only be placed on a Singh the Khalsa itself judges worthy.
